title: Mistral Releases Le Chonk, a 1 Trillion Parameter Open Weight Model
key_facts: Mistral AI unveiled Mistral Large 4 on 6 Oct, a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 1.05 trillion total and 49 billion active parameters, per the company's announcement.
It is in public preview in Mistral's API at $1.36 per million input tokens and $4.18 per million output tokens; GPT-5.5 is listed at $5.00 and $30.00.
Open weights are due on 31 Oct (a caption in the article says 27 Oct); the licence is not final, terms 'coming soon'.
Simon Willison, who tested it, flagged that the API offers only two reasoning levels, 'none' and 'high'.
On Artificial Analysis's index it scored 38, behind DeepSeek's 4.1 Flash (552 billion parameters).
It trails Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.5 on hard reasoning and agentic benchmarks such as Terminal-Bench and Humanity's Last Exam.
Mistral claims it leads AutomationBench at about a fifth of rivals' per-task cost and positions it for coding, cybersecurity and corporate workflows.
quote_evidence: Mistral hasn't finalized the license yet. Its announcement says terms are "coming soon."
Mistral Large 4 trails well behind frontier closed models like Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.5 on hard reasoning and agentic benchmarks
The full open weights release is set for October 31.
why_it_matters_hint: A European lab plans to give away a trillion-parameter model's weights, which matters to organisations that want to keep data out of US-run APIs.
notes: Launch is 8 days old; article is a follow-on piece. Article is internally inconsistent: weights date 31 Oct vs 27 Oct in a caption; 3,800 vs 4,000 GPUs. Both left out of the summary. Price and benchmark claims are the company's.
